acceptance_criteria: AC199-1: Consume the exact supported immutable capability and actual API from MT-198. Perform the actual native GUI migration with coherent dependency/lock adoption under Primary custody. Adapt inspected startup/render ownership without replacing unrelated libraries or editing canonical internals from a host-only lease.

AC199-2: Prove the genuine running Handshake app uses a Vulkan adapter/backend with exact binary/source/dependency/config identity, real frames and resize/minimize/restore/surface recovery. Configuration, a build, a prototype or D3D/OpenGL fallback does not prove Vulkan.

AC199-3: Preserve keyboard/focus/IME, DPI/multiwindow, accessibility, correct rendering, quiet behavior, diagnostics and model-use routes. Explicit platform limitations cannot silently replace original required behavior.

AC199-4: GUI coder B owns the disjoint external vulkan-renderer candidate. Coordinate shared app/lib/manifest integration with coder A and Primary as exact sequential hook handoff. Original runtime/process/finite-pool limits remain unchanged.

AC199-5: Adopt Vulkan through the authoritative shared GPU owner and focused typed client/ownership contract, with accountable allocations/budgets/pressure/staging/shared-versus-dedicated/inflight/reclaim/shutdown/device-loss/recovery/multiwindow/module attach/detach. Prove genuine Vulkan backend/device and required lifecycle behavior; no renamed DX/OpenGL fallback or independent per-module pool bypass. MT-203 owns the central host lifecycle contract and scoped evidence.

AC199-6: Actual Vulkan backend/device, native GUI action/error and affected GPU memory/lifetime failures are observable through existing internal_diagnostics and correlated standalone Palmistry records, under original allowlist/privacy. Neither a source declaration nor configured backend label proves event wiring or crash survival.
